answer.generated: Dynamic scheduling can eliminate data hazards by reordering instructions to avoid stalls caused by output and antidependences, where one instruction depends on the result of another before it completes. This approach also addresses control hazards, such as speculative execution of branches, by dynamically speculating outcomes based on branch predictions. By renaming registers and issuing multiple instructions per cycle, dynamic scheduling reduces stalls and improves instruction-level parallelism.
